data.theme: Generic and Professional Competencies in Engineering Education
data.definition: The assessment and development of non-technical or transferable skills (e.g., communication, teamwork, leadership, problem-solving) essential for professional success in engineering. This includes workplace readiness and the integration of internship-based learning to enhance these competencies.

data.theme: Self-Efficacy and Attitudinal Measurement in Engineering Contexts
data.definition: The development and validation of instruments to measure students' self-efficacy (confidence in performing specific tasks) and attitudes toward various aspects of engineering. This includes entrepreneurial self-efficacy and self-perception of competence in practical work settings.

The use of rubrics as structured assessment tools to evaluate specific competencies in engineering students, particularly in laboratory, project-based, or practical settings. Emphasis is placed on expert judgment, inter-rater reliability, and performance assessment.

data.theme: Research Competencies and Investigative Skills in Engineering Students
data.definition: The assessment and development of research-related competencies in engineering students, including intellectual, technical, and communicative skills necessary for conducting and presenting research. This encompasses research training, scientific writing, and data collection techniques.

The exploration of factors contributing to the development of engineering identity in students, such as self-efficacy, recognition, interest, and interpersonal skills. This theme examines how students perceive themselves within the engineering profession.

data.theme: Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving in Engineering
data.definition: The development and validation of instruments to assess critical thinking and problem-solving skills in engineering students, often within specific technical domains. This includes representational competence, design problem-solving, and reflective thinking.

data.theme: Transversal and Sociotechnical Competencies in Engineering
data.definition: The assessment of transversal competencies (e.g., teamwork, lifelong learning, entrepreneurial skills) and sociotechnical competencies (e.g., understanding social implications of technology). This theme also addresses affective domain assessment in engineering education.
